page: UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-1xL40S is a GPU-accelerated and memory-dense cloud instance hosted on KVM. The instance integrates an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9575F processor providing 20 physical cores and 20 vCPUs at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz with one thread per core under a shared CPU allocation model. Compute capabilities are augmented by hardware instruction support including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, AES, and SHA extensions. Graphics and tensor processing are powered by a single NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S GPU equipped with 48 GB of GDDR6 VRAM. The system features 256 GB of system RAM, yielding a high memory density of 12.8 GB per core. No local storage is included with the instance, requiring external block storage for persistent data, and one complimentary public IPv4 address is provided.

Benchmark results indicate strong computational and memory performance across diverse workloads. In synthetic CPU tests, single-core execution reached top-tier standing with a stress-ng score of 4,189.09 and a Geekbench single-core result of 2,165.0, alongside top-tier single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 17.93 GB/sec. Multi-core performance remained in the upper tier with a stress-ng output of 84,015.49 and a PassMark CPU score of 62,326.31, while multi-threaded Geekbench achieved an average tier result of 15,797.0. The memory subsystem demonstrated high read throughput of 309.72 GB/sec and write throughput of 135.97 GB/sec for uncached blocks, coupled with 85.33 million Redis SET operations per second. Hardware acceleration via the NVIDIA L40S GPU yielded top-tier LLM inference on small 135M parameter models with 4,434.62 prompt tokens per second and 386.89 text generation tokens per second, with solid generation speeds of 36.85 tokens per second on 7B parameter models, tapering to 3.97 tokens per second on 70B models.

The lack of integrated local storage necessitates architectural planning around networked storage volumes, which can introduce latency tradeoffs for data-heavy pipelines. However, the generous 256 GB host RAM footprint and dedicated 48 GB GPU VRAM provide exceptional resource density for memory-bound tasks. This instance profile is well aligned for small- to medium-scale LLM inference, AI fine-tuning, image and video processing, GPU-accelerated data science, in-memory caching layers, and compute-heavy analytical services.
description: The UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-1xL40S is a GPU-accelerated cloud instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor featuring 20 vCPUs and 20 physical cores running at 2.0 GHz on a shared allocation model. It is configured with 256 GB of system RAM, delivering 12.8 GB per core, and is paired with a single NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S GPU with 48 GB of VRAM. The server includes no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage for disk operations, and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Benchmarks demonstrate top-tier single-core CPU throughput and strong memory bandwidth alongside robust AI inference capabilities, delivering 386.89 tokens per second on small language models and 36.85 tokens per second on medium models. With its combination of extensive system memory and high-capacity GPU acceleration, this configuration is well suited for machine learning inference, computer vision, data analytics, and memory-intensive processing pipelines.
